bibliographic.title: Employee-Driven Leakage of Technical Documentation into General-Purpose LLMs: An Integrative Review
bibliographic.authors: Latinović, L., Zhukovskiy, O., Mašić, O., & Živković, D.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Latinović, L., Zhukovskiy, O., Mašić, O., & Živković, D. (2026). Employee-driven leakage of technical documentation into general-purpose LLMs: An integrative review. Serbian Journal of Engineering Management, 11(1), 77. https://doi.org/10.5937/SJEM2601077L

methodology.study_design: integrative review synthesizing peer-reviewed research, provider and regulator materials, and structured incident reporting
methodology.sample_description: heterogeneous corpus spanning peer-reviewed literature on LLM use in work settings, provider documentation, and structured incident databases/case reports
methodology.sector: engineering and documentation work / enterprise knowledge work
methodology.technology_context: general-purpose LLMs used by employees via chat/API/plugin for interpreting standards, troubleshooting, and drafting engineering artefacts

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper is an integrative review focused on employee-driven leakage of technical documentation into general-purpose LLMs and proposes an auditable governance approach with a minimal guardrail stack. It is relevant to operational LLM governance, observability, compliance, and escalation, but it is not centered on conversational AI systems or conversational governance in regulated high-stakes domains.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Provided text is partial (front matter, methodology fragments, references); Python-extracted bibliographic metadata was garbled and year may differ from journal issue (2026).

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on partial text. Integrative review design and inclusion criteria are stated, but full search, screening, and synthesis procedures are not visible in the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The review presents a coherent mechanism map and governance framework with explicit limitations, but available text does not fully document search and synthesis procedures, and the study addresses organizational LLM data-governance rather than conversational governance in regulated conversational systems.

coding.theme: Organizational governance of employee LLM use
coding.subtheme: Documentation leakage pathways and proportionate guardrails

synthesis.main_claim: Routine employee use of general-purpose LLMs creates bidirectional flows that externalize proprietary documentation and reintroduce model outputs into internal systems, concentrating risk at specific transition points where observability is often weakest.
synthesis.contribution: Synthesizes heterogeneous evidence into a mechanism map of employee-driven documentation leakage and proposes a proportionate minimal guardrail stack plus an organizational evaluation framework with auditable metrics such as consolidation onto sanctioned channels, blocking effectiveness, and policy-drift lag.
synthesis.limitations: The paper explicitly does not assert prevalence and aims to make assumptions explicit; full prevalence estimates and complete review methods are not evidenced in the provided excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on operational LLM governance, guardrails, observability, compliance, and escalation for employee LLM workflows; limited direct value as central evidence on conversational AI governance in regulated conversational systems.

evidence.claim: Focus is general-purpose LLMs used by employees in engineering/documentation work
evidence.excerpt: General-purpose large language models are increasingly used by employees to interpret standards, troubleshoot systems, and draft or refine engineering artefacts.

evidence.claim: Identifies boundary-crossing transition points where risk and weak observability concentrate
evidence.excerpt: We identify a recurrent set of boundary-crossing transition points such as copy–paste, upload/OCR, connector invocation, and paste-back, where risk concentrates and where observability is often weakest.

evidence.claim: Proposes auditable governance with a minimal guardrail stack and evaluation metrics
evidence.excerpt: we propose a proportionate “minimal guardrail stack” and an organisational evaluation framework combining qualitative risk scoring, rule-based escalation, and simple, trackable metrics
